[[File:Caeleb Dressel before winning 100 fly (42769914221).jpg|thumb|right|270px|[[Caeleb Dressel]] (pictured) holds the most world records in men's swimming with four (two individual and two relays). [[Léon Marchand]] holds the most individual world records, with three.]]
[[File:Katie Ledecky Olympics 2016b.jpg|alt=|thumb|270px|[[Katie Ledecky]] (pictured) holds two long course world records (three total). [[Kate Douglass]] (five individual and six relays) holds the most world records, with eleven. [[Summer McIntosh]] holds the most individual world records, with seven.]]

The '''world records in swimming''' are ratified by [[World Aquatics]] (formerly known as FINA), the international governing body of swimming. Records can be set in [[long course]] (50 metres) or [[Short course (swimming)|short course]] (25 metres) swimming pools. World Aquatics recognizes world records in the following events for both men and women,<ref name="FINA SW12">{{cite web|url=http://www.fina.org/project/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=45&Itemid=119 |title=FINA Technical Rules SW12.1 and 12.2 |publisher=[[International Swimming Federation]] |access-date=11 May 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130726002347/http://www.fina.org/project/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=45&Itemid=119 |archive-date=26 July 2013 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://fina.org/H2O/docs/WR_July_27_2015.pdf |title=FINA World Records |publisher=[[FINA]] |date=27 July 2015 |access-date=16 September 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150913213741/http://www.fina.org/H2O/docs/WR_July_27_2015.pdf |archive-date=13 September 2015 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }}</ref> except for the mixed relays, where teams consist of two men and two women, in any order.
* Freestyle: [[World record progression 50 metres freestyle|50m]], [[World record progression 100 metres freestyle|100m]], [[World record progression 200 metres freestyle|200m]], [[World record progression 400 metres freestyle|400m]], [[World record progression 800 metres freestyle|800m]], [[World record progression 1500 metres freestyle|1500m]]
* Backstroke: [[World record progression 50 metres backstroke|50m]], [[World record progression 100 metres backstroke|100m]], [[World record progression 200 metres backstroke|200m]]
* Breaststroke: [[World record progression 50 metres breaststroke|50m]], [[World record progression 100 metres breaststroke|100m]], [[World record progression 200 metres breaststroke|200m]]
* Butterfly: [[World record progression 50 metres butterfly|50m]], [[World record progression 100 metres butterfly|100m]], [[World record progression 200 metres butterfly|200m]]
* Individual medley: [[World record progression 100 metres individual medley|100m]] (short course only), [[World record progression 200 metres individual medley|200m]], [[World record progression 400 metres individual medley|400m]]
* Relays: [[World record progression 4 × 50 metres freestyle relay|4 × 50 m freestyle relay]] (short course only), [[World record progression 4 × 100 metres freestyle relay|4 × 100 m freestyle]], [[World record progression 4 × 200 metres freestyle relay|4 × 200 m freestyle]], [[World record progression 4 × 50 metres medley relay|4 × 50 m medley relay]] (short course only), [[World record progression 4 × 100 metres medley relay|4 × 100 m medley]]
* Mixed relays: [[World record progression 4 × 50 metres freestyle relay#Mixed|4 × 50 m mixed freestyle]] (short course only), [[World record progression 4 × 100 metres freestyle relay#Mixed|4 × 100 m mixed freestyle]] (long course only), [[World record progression 4 × 50 metres medley relay#Mixed|4 × 50 m mixed medley]] (short course only), [[World record progression 4 × 100 metres medley relay#Mixed|4 × 100 m mixed medley]] (long course only)<ref name="WA-record-rules-2026" />

The ratification process is described in FINA Rule SW12,<ref name="FINA SW12" /> and involves submission of paperwork certifying the accuracy of the timing system and the length of the pool, satisfaction of FINA rules regarding swimwear and a negative doping test by the swimmer(s) involved. Records can be set at intermediate distances in an individual race and for the first leg of a relay race. Records which have not yet been fully ratified are marked with a '#' symbol in these lists.

Some of the records below were established by swimmers wearing [[High-technology swimwear fabric|bodysuits or suits made of polyurethane or other non-textile materials]] allowed in the race pool from February 2008 until December 2009. On the eve of the [[2009 World Aquatics Championships|2009 FINA World Championships]] in Rome, the international governing body for five Olympic aquatic sports voted to ban the use of bodysuits and all suits made of non-textile materials starting 1 January 2010.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.timeslive.co.za/sport/other/2010/01/18/high-tech-records-to-stand|title=High-tech records to stand|date=18 January 2010|access-date=27 July 2011|publisher=Times Live|archive-date=17 March 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120317191633/http://www.timeslive.co.za/sport/other/2010/01/18/high-tech-records-to-stand|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2009-jul-25-sp-world-swimming25-story.html|title=FINA bans bodysuits that have led to spate of world records|last=Dillman|first=Lisa|date=25 July 2009|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|access-date=27 July 2011|archive-date=9 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201109032432/https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2009-jul-25-sp-world-swimming25-story.html|url-status=live}}</ref> The suits seemed to improve the performance in those with larger physiques, boosting performance in some athletes more than others,{{who|date=September 2015}} depending on [[Morphology (biology)|morphology]] and physiology.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://abcnews.go.com/Sports/wireStory?id=13900301|title=New Suits Mean No More Records in Swimming|date=22 June 2011|last=Dampf|first=Andrew|access-date=27 July 2011|publisher=ABC News}}</ref> Since then, [[List of textile best times in swimming|best times set by swimmers wearing textile materials]] have once again overtaken more than half of the world records recognized by World Aquatics.

On 25 July 2013, FINA Technical Swimming Congress voted to allow world records in the long course mixed 400 free relay and mixed 400 medley relay, as well as in six events in short course metres: the mixed 200 medley and 200 free relays, as well as the men's and women's 200 free relays and the men's and women's 200 medley relays.<ref>{{cite web|title=FINA Swimming Rules 2013 – 2017 incl. World Record Application Form|url=http://www.fina.org/H2O/docs/rules/sw_rules_20132017_inclwrform.pdf|publisher=[[FINA]]|date=16 August 2013|access-date=27 September 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150824112202/http://www.fina.org/H2O/docs/rules/sw_rules_20132017_inclwrform.pdf|archive-date=24 August 2015|df=dmy-all}}</ref> In October 2013, FINA decided to establish "standards" before something can be recognized as the first World Record in these events.<ref>{{cite news|title=FINA To Set World Best Standards For Mixed Relays|url=http://www.swimvortex.com/fina-to-set-world-best-standards-for-mixed-relays/|work=swimvortex.com|author=Craig Lord|date=3 October 2013|access-date=5 December 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151208091537/http://www.swimvortex.com/fina-to-set-world-best-standards-for-mixed-relays/|archive-date=8 December 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> But later on 13 March 2014 FINA has officially ratified the eight world records set by Indiana University swimmers at the IU Relay Rally held on 26 September 2013 in Bloomington.<ref>{{cite magazine|title=FINA Goes Back in Time to Ratify Indiana Hoosier Swims as World Records|url=http://www.swimmingworldmagazine.com/lane9/news/World/38199.asp?q=FINA-Goes-Back-in-Time-to-Ratify-Indiana-Hoosier-Swims-as-World-Records|magazine=[[Swimming World Magazine]]|date=13 March 2014|access-date=5 December 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140705174106/http://www.swimmingworldmagazine.com/lane9/news/World/38199.asp?q=FINA-Goes-Back-in-Time-to-Ratify-Indiana-Hoosier-Swims-as-World-Records|archive-date=5 July 2014|df=dmy-all}}</ref>

==World bests and other relay performances==
World Aquatics recognises mixed 4 × 100 m freestyle and medley relay world records in 50 m pools, and mixed 4 × 50 m freestyle and medley relay world records in 25 m pools. For a relay world record to be recognised, all team members must have the same sporting nationality.<ref name="WA-record-rules-2026">{{cite web |title=World Aquatics Competition Regulations |url=https://resources.fina.org/fina/document/2026/02/18/e6815ecc-06d9-4f0b-98e9-4c441cf5e6a3/2026-02-18_World-Aquatics_CR-Final.pdf |publisher=World Aquatics |date=18 February 2026 |at=p. 65, Part Two, articles 12.1–12.3.3 |access-date=11 September 2026}}</ref>

The tables below list documented world bests and championship or league records that are not ratified World Aquatics world records.
